slides.say: A, B and C represent digits. Given: C B, times B, is equal to A C B. Which of the following could be B?
So a multiplication in letters, and we look for B. [short pause] Let's write it vertically and look at the ones column.

B times B ends in B. A digit times itself that keeps its units digit. That happens only for four digits, zero, one, five and six. Zero times zero is zero, one times one is one, five times five is twenty-five, and six times six is thirty-six. These are the special digits.
No other digit does it. Seven times seven is forty-nine, and four times four is sixteen. So choice numbers one and four are out.

Two more facts about them. Five times an even number ends in zero, five times four is twenty. Five times an odd number ends in five, five times three is fifteen. And six times an even number keeps that number's units digit. Six times four is twenty-four, and six times eight is forty-eight.
Five or zero are left. Zero? Zero times anything is zero, not a three-digit number. Out.
So B is five, and it really works. Twenty-five times five is one twenty-five. Choice number two is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
